arxiv-1804-05995.title: Structuring Wikipedia Articles with Section Recommendations Conference: The 41st International ACM SIGIR Conference on Research & Development in Information Retrieval; July 8–12, 2018; Ann Arbor, MI, USA SIGIR ’18: The 41st International ACM SIGIR Conference on Research & Development in Information
arxiv-1804-05995.creator: Tiziano Piccardi, Michele Catasta, Leila Zia, Robert West
arxiv-1804-05995.description: A 2018 arXiv research paper by Tiziano Piccardi, Michele Catasta, Leila Zia, Robert West. Sections are the building blocks of Wikipedia articles. They enhance readability and can be used as a structured entry point for creating and expanding articles. Structuring a new or already existing Wikipedia article with sections is a hard task for humans, especially for newcomers or less experienced editors, as it requires significant knowledge about how a well-written article looks for each possible topic.

arxiv-2102-06981.title: DNA codes over two noncommutative rings of order four
arxiv-2102-06981.creator: Jon-Lark Kim Dong Eun Ohk
arxiv-2102-06981.description: Abstract In this paper, we describe a new type of DNA codes over two noncommutative rings E E and F F of order four with characteristic 2. Our DNA codes are based on quasi self-dual codes over E E and F F .

arxiv-2302-09120.title: Robot path planning using deep reinforcement learning
arxiv-2302-09120.creator: Miguel Quiñones-Ramírez, Jorge Ríos-Martínez, Víctor Uc-Cetina
arxiv-2302-09120.description: Abstract Autonomous navigation is challenging for mobile robots, especially in an unknown environment. Commonly, the robot requires multiple sensors to map the environment, locate itself, and make a plan to reach the target. However, reinforcement learning methods offer an alternative to map-free navigation tasks by learning the optimal actions to take.

arxiv-2304-05870.title: COMPLEXITY AND SIMPLICITY OF SELF–GRAVITATING FLUIDS
arxiv-2304-05870.creator: L. Herrera
arxiv-2304-05870.description: Abstract We review a recently proposed definition of complexity of the structure of self–gravitating fluids ch1 , and the criterium to define the simplest mode of their evolution ch2 ; rg5 . We analyze the origin of these concepts and their possible applications in the study of gravitation collapse.

arxiv-2310-09419.title: Spectral Moment Formulae for G ​ L ​ ( 3 ) × G ​ L ​ ( 2 ) GL(3)\times GL(2) L L -functions II: The Eisenstein Case
arxiv-2310-09419.creator: Chung-Hang Kwan
arxiv-2310-09419.description: Abstract . This is a sequel to Kwan [ Kw23 ] . We continue our investigations on the spectral moments of L L -functions of G ​ L ​ ( 3 ) × G ​ L ​ ( 2 ) GL(3)\times GL(2) -type from the perspective of period integrals.

arxiv-2311-16744.title: Blockchain-based Zero Trust on the Edge
arxiv-2311-16744.creator: Cem Bicer, Ilir Murturi, Praveen Kumar Donta, Schahram Dustdar
arxiv-2311-16744.description: Abstract Internet of Things (IoT) devices pose significant security challenges due to their heterogeneity (i.e., hardware and software) and vulnerability to extensive attack surfaces. Today’s conventional perimeter-based systems use credential-based authentication (e.g., username/password, certificates, etc.) to decide whether an actor can access a network.

arxiv-2402-16981.title: Non-Euclidean Sliced Optimal Transport Sampling Volume: 43 Issue: 2
arxiv-2402-16981.creator: Baptiste Genest 1 , Nicolas Courty 2 and David Coeurjolly 1 1 Univ Lyon, CNRS, Lyon1, INSA, LIRIS, France 2 Université Bretagne Sud, IRISA, CNRS, France
arxiv-2402-16981.description: Abstract In machine learning and computer graphics, a fundamental task is the approximation of a probability density function through a well-dispersed collection of samples. Providing a formal metric for measuring the distance between probability measures on general spaces, Optimal Transport (OT) emerges as a pivotal theoretical framework within this context.

arxiv-2505-22896.title: Exploring Integration by Differentiation
arxiv-2505-22896.creator: R. D. George and C. Vignat
arxiv-2505-22896.description: Abstract This work validates and extends the method of integration by differentiation, initially introduced by A. Kempf et al., and demonstrates its compatibility with classical rules of integration. It provides applications to classical integrals, including one by Ramanujan, and extends the method to the multivariate setting.

arxiv-2507-01703.title: The SOFIA Massive (SOMA) Star Formation Q-band Follow-up. II.
arxiv-2507-01703.creator: Prasanta Gorai ,, Kotomi Taniguchi, Jonathan C. Tan, Miguel G o ´ \acute{\rm{o}} mez-Garrido, Viviana Rosero, Izaskun Jim´enez-Serra, Yichen Zhang, Giuliana Cosentino, Chi-Yan Law, Rubén Fedriani, Gemma Busquet, Brandt A. L. Gaches, Maryam Saberi, Ankan Das
arxiv-2507-01703.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Prasanta Gorai ,, Kotomi Taniguchi, Jonathan C. Tan, Miguel G o ´ \acute{\rm{o}} mez-Garrido, Viviana Rosero, Izaskun Jim´enez-Serra, Yichen Zhang, Giuliana Cosentino, Chi-Yan Law, Rubén Fedriani, Gemma Busquet, Brandt A. L. Gaches, Maryam Saberi, Ankan Das. Hydrogen recombination lines (HRLs) are valuable diagnostics of the physical conditions in ionized regions surrounding high-mass stars. Understanding these lines, including broadening mechanisms and intensity trends, can provide insights into HII region densities, temperatures, and kinematics.

arxiv-2510-24922.title: Simulating Turbulent Wakes without the Upstream Body
arxiv-2510-24922.creator: Zhicheng Wang 1 Theo Käufer 2 Khemraj Shukla 1 Michael Triantafyllou 2, George Em Karniadakis 1
arxiv-2510-24922.description: Abstract We present a simplified framework for simulating three-dimensional turbulent wakes without the upstream body that generates them. Instead of resolving the geometry, the incompressible Navier–Stokes equations are solved in a rectangular domain on which the inflow boundary condition is prescribed as either phase-averaged or time-averaged velocity profiles obtained from experimental measurements and direct numerical simulations.

arxiv-2511-07410.title: Using Vision Language Models as Closed-Loop Symbolic Planners for Robotic Applications: A Control-Theoretic Perspective
arxiv-2511-07410.creator: Hao Wang, Sathwik Karnik, Beatrice Lim, Somil Bansal
arxiv-2511-07410.description: Abstract Large Language Models (LLMs) and Vision Language Models (VLMs) have been widely used for embodied symbolic planning. Yet, how to effectively use these models for closed-loop symbolic planning remains largely unexplored. Because they operate as black boxes, LLMs and VLMs can produce unpredictable or costly errors, making their use in high-level robotic planning especially challenging.

arxiv-2511-13550.title: MDIntrinsicDimension: Dimensionality-Based Analysis of Collective Motions in Macromolecules from Molecular Dynamics Trajectories
arxiv-2511-13550.creator: Irene Cazzaniga, Toni Giorgino
arxiv-2511-13550.description: Abstract Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations provide atomistic insights into the structure, dynamics, and function of biomolecules by generating time-resolved, high-dimensional trajectories. Analyzing such data benefits from estimating the minimal number of variables required to describe the explored conformational manifold, known as the intrinsic dimension (ID).

arxiv-2603-02327.title: Not all nitrogen-rich field stars originate from globular clusters
arxiv-2603-02327.creator: E. I. Leitinger, A. Miglio, J. Montalbán, D. Massari, A. Bragaglia, W. E. van Rossem, K. Brogaard, A. Mazzi, J. S. Thomsen, E. Willett

In Trypanosoma cruzi, the causative agent of Chagas disease, the mitochondrial genome has a unique structural organization consisting of 20-50 maxicircles (∼20 kb) and...

pmc-10572872.title: SINEs as Potential Expression Cassettes: Impact of Deletions and Insertions on Polyadenylation and Lifetime of B2 and Ves SINE Transcripts Generated by RNA Polymerase III
pmc-10572872.creator: Olga R Borodulina, Ilia G Ustyantsev, Dmitri A Kramerov, Irmgard Tegeder
pmc-10572872.description: Short Interspersed Elements (SINEs) are common in the genomes of most multicellular organisms. They are transcribed by RNA polymerase III from an internal promoter comprising boxes A and B. As transcripts of certain SINEs from mammalian genomes can be polyadenylated, such transcripts should contain the AATAAA sequence as well as those called β- and τ-signals.

pmc-10669903.title: POD-Galerkin FSI Analysis for Flapping Motion
pmc-10669903.creator: Shigeki Kaneko, Shinobu Yoshimura, Jiang Zhao
pmc-10669903.description: FSI simulations of flapping motions have been widely investigated to develop a flapping-wing micro air vehicle. Because an intensive parametric study is important for the product design, a computationally efficient model is required. The purpose of the present study was to develop a reduced-order model of flapping motion.

pmc-11303545.title: SRS-Net: a universal framework for solving stimulated Raman scattering in nonlinear fiber-optic systems by physics-informed deep learning
pmc-11303545.creator: Yuchen Song, Min Zhang, Xiaotian Jiang, Fan Zhang, Cheng Ju, Shanguo Huang, Alan Pak Tao Lau, Danshi Wang
pmc-11303545.description: As a crucial nonlinear phenomenon, stimulated Raman scattering (SRS) plays multifaceted roles involved in forward and inverse problems. In fibre-optic systems, these roles range from detrimental interference that impairs optical performance to beneficial effects that enables various devices such as Raman amplifier. To obtain solutions of SRS, various numerical methods customized for different scenarios have been proposed.

pmc-11369259.title: Assessment of portable X-ray fluorescence (pXRF) for plant-available nutrient prediction in biochar-amended soils
pmc-11369259.creator: Joao Antonangelo, Hailin Zhang
pmc-11369259.description: Portable X-ray Fluorescence probe (pXRF) is a tool used to measure many elements quickly and efficiently in soil with minimal sample preparation. Although this sensing technique has been widely used to determine total elemental concentrations, it has not been calibrated for plant-available nutrient predictions. We evaluated the potential of using pXRF for fast plant-available nutrient quantification.

pmc-11499886.title: Randomised controlled trial comparing different intersession intervals of intermittent theta burst delivered to the dorsal medial prefrontal cortex
pmc-11499886.creator: Michelle S Goodman, Laura Schulze, Zafiris J Daskalakis, Gerasimos N Konstantinou, Farrokh Mansouri, Alisson P Trevizol, Daniel M Blumberger, Jonathan Downar
pmc-11499886.description: BackgroundIntermittent theta burst stimulation (iTBS) is a form of repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) that can be administered in a fraction of the time of standard rTMS. Applying multiple daily iTBS sessions (ie, accelerated iTBS) may enable patients to achieve remission more rapidly. However, questions remain regarding the optimal time interval between treatment sessions.

pmc-11710453.title: Evaluate the Efficacy of the Axl inhibitor Bemcentinib in the 5xFAD mouse model of Alzheimer’s Disease
pmc-11710453.creator: Guyin Chen, Gizem Ozturk, Sílvia Porta, Virginia M‐Y Lee
pmc-11710453.description: BackgroundAlzheimer’s disease (AD) is a neurodegenerative disease characterized by the presence of phosphorylated tau neurofibrillary tangles and extracellular deposits of amyloid beta plaques (Aβ) in the brain. Microglia cells have been proposed to be involved in amyloid plaque formation since activated microglia produce inflammatory cytokines that contribute to a hostile neuronal environment, exacerbating AD pathogenesis.

pmc-12526916.title: Flow-Line-Reducing Tetrahedral Metal Effect Pigments for Injection Molding: A Yield-Rate-Improved Particle Manufacturing Method Based on Soft UVImprint Lithography
pmc-12526916.creator: Nils Maximilian Demski, Holger Seidlitz, Felix Kuke, Oliver Niklas Dorn, Janina Zoglauer, Tobias Hückstaedt, Paul Hans Kamm, Francisco García-Moreno, Noah Kremp, Christian Dreyer, Dirk Oberschmidt
pmc-12526916.description: This publication presents an improved manufacturing method for tetrahedral metal effect pigment particles that demonstrates reduced flowlines in injection-molded polymer components compared with conventional platelet-shaped pigment particles. The previously published cold forming process for tetrahedral particles, made entirely from aluminum, faced manufacturing challenges, resulting in a high reject rate due to particle adhesion to the micro-structured mold roller.

pmc-12549911.title: Identification and characterization of tissue- and stress-specific circular RNAs (circRNAs) of tea to generate the largest tea circRNAs data repository
pmc-12549911.creator: Hukam C Rawal, Ranit Kumar Pal, Tapan Kumar Mondal
pmc-12549911.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Enormous RNA-seq data of tea (Camellia sinensis) is available at NCBI, yet only 3,174 circular RNAs (circRNAs) have been reported to date. This study establishes a foundation for using public datasets to generate circRNA reservoirs. After standardizing the pipeline using in-house RNA-seq data from Indian tea, 178 RNA-seq datasets of tea were downloaded from NCBI and used for the generation of the largest tissue and stress-specific tea circRNAs repository (TCDB; http://indianteagenome.in:8080/tcdb/), till date.

pmc-13069115.title: Balancing the efficacy and safety of chimeric antigen receptor T-cell therapy by affinity combination
pmc-13069115.creator: Linda Warmuth, Sarah Dötsch, Manuel Trebo, Sarah Bellucci, Sophia Engels, Rafael Valdivia Manrique, Karl Moukarzel, Julius M. Schütz, Monika Hammel, Adrian Straub, Sabrina Wagner, Anna Hochholzer, Ciro Salinno, Jacqueline Seigner, Charlotte U. Zajc, Georg P. Schmidt, Josefine Michael, Thomas Nerrete
pmc-13069115.description: Recent studies suggest that Chimeric Antigen Receptor (CAR) binding affinity to its ligand affects CAR-T-cell functionality. Affinity engineering towards lower binding strengths might mitigate therapeutic side effects arising from intense CAR-T-cell activation as well as tumor relapse due to antigen-escape or limited persistence of CAR-T cells during sustained activation via high-affinity receptors.

pmc-13146274.title: ABSTRACT NUMBER: ESOC2026A438 EARLY DETECTION OF PEDIATRIC FAMILIAL HYPERCHOLESTEROLEMIA THROUGH REVERSE CASCADE SCREENING AND STROKE RISK SIGNALS: PRELIMINARY RESULTS FROM THE EPIRUS PROJECT

pmc-13146274.description: Background and aimsFamilial hypercholesterolemia (FH) is associated with lifelong exposure to elevated LDL-cholesterol and a markedly increased risk of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD). The EPIRUS FH Reverse Cascade Project applies targeted family-based screening in Northwestern Greece, enabling pediatric identification and assessment of vascular risk, including cerebrovascular events.

pmc-13561026.title: Therapeut:innen-Augmentation durch generative KI: Konzept und Umsetzung des GAINED-Feedback-Systems an der Universität Osnabrück
pmc-13561026.creator: Christopher Lalk, Tobias Steinbrenner, Julian Rubel
pmc-13561026.description: Die zunehmende Verbreitung von generativer KI ermöglicht neue Anwendungsfelder in der Psychotherapie. Dazu zählen 1. Chatbots für eine direkte Interaktion der Patient:innen mit einer KI, 2. Trainingsanwendungen für Therapeuten, bei denen Therapeut:innen mit simulierten KI-Patienten üben können und 3. Augmentationsanwendungen, bei denen Therapeut:innen durch automatisierte Dokumentation oder Feedback- und Entscheidungshilfen unterstützt werden.
